- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at +3–5% above prior high.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or bearish; if forecast is rising >1.5% per day, reduce slope by 0.1–0.3% per day.
- When official events are frequent and supply net is negative, model tends to ignore event impact; add 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to forecast if >10 events/30d.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., 1.00 or 0.50) followed by low prices, model often fails to reset; force 3–5 day lag correction to align with true low.
